notes: All parts exist in the catalogue, so no lookup or new part types were needed.

Each LED sits in two adjacent columns in the top half of the breadboard (anode at columns 7, 10, 13, 16, 19, 22; cathode in the next column). A 220 ohm resistor bridges the centre gap in the anode column, and a blue jumper runs from the Arduino pin to that column's bottom half.
Arduino pins 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2 feed LEDs 1 to 6, left to right, as in the image.
Each LED cathode goes through a short black jumper to the top negative rail, and one black wire joins that rail to the Arduino GND next to pin 13/AREF. I used GND.1 for it.
Breadboard row letters follow the catalogue naming (top half = bank t, bottom half = bank b). The exact row in each strip is arbitrary because all holes in a strip are connected.
The schematic and image show only 220 ohm resistors with no pull-ups or other parts, so none were added.
